verdict.rationale: Supabase documents daily backups for Pro/Team/Enterprise plans (supabase-docs-11) and a branching feature for creating isolated preview/test environments off production (supabase-docs-26, supabase-docs-36), but the evidence pack never documents true point-in-time recovery (restoring to an arbitrary timestamp within a retention window) or branching a database from a specific point in time to recover from bad writes — branching here is framed as a dev/test tool, not a recovery mechanism. A historical community report even notes backups relied on pg_dump with the CEO saying they'd 'investigate moving users to PITR' (supabase-comm-4), suggesting PITR was not the default recovery model at that time. missing for 10: explicit PITR documentation, ability to branch/restore to an arbitrary timestamp, retention-window guarantees, and confirmation that branching can be used specifically for bad-write recovery rather than just feature development.
